nodes.label: Redis master pod exceeded its 512Mi memory limit and was OOMKilled, causing downstream connection failures

grounding.query: redis-master pod OOMKilled 512Mi connection refused celery-worker checkout-svc 503
grounding.answer: The sources indicate that the redis-master pod was OOMKilled due to insufficient memory, with a configured memory limit of 250Mi. The celery-worker pod was also OOMKilled, with a memory limit of 512Mi. The celery worker may have encountered connection refusals to Redis due to it restarting before Redis became available, as noted in discussions about similar issues in Kubernetes environments. The sources also mention that resource limits and network connectivity issues can cause OOMKilled statuses and connection refusals.

NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE  
celery-worker-abc123 0/1 OOMKilled 3 5m
Diagnose:

# Check resource usage  
kubectl top pods -n your-namespace | grep celery# Check limits  
kubectl get deployment celery-worker -n your-namespace \  
 -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers.resources}'
Fix:

resources:

remediation_plan: Increase Redis master memory limit and resource requests
Review and adjust resource quotas for redis and celery pods
Implement pod restart and disruption policies
Monitor memory metrics and set proactive alerts
Validate application-level reconnection and retry logic
